sections.title: Overview
sections.content: This document contains an analysis of performance bottlenecks in the brain visualization application, focusing on model loading, rendering performance, state management, and component design patterns.

sections.title: Zustand Store Architecture Analysis
sections.content: The current Zustand store implementation (useAppStore.ts) presents several performance challenges.

strengths: Uses slice pattern to organize state into logical domains (ModelsSlice, UiSlice, etc.)
Employs specialized selectors for better component performance
Has memory optimization like clearCache to help with resource management
Uses shallow comparison for object equality in some cases
weaknesses: State Structure Issues: Combines UI state with large 3D model references
Circular Reference Risk: Store references to THREE.js objects directly
Inefficient Selector Pattern: Some selectors return new object references, triggering re-renders
Non-optimized Action Functions: Many state updates are not batch-optimized
Missing Memoization: Some action function references are recreated on each render
Incomplete Cleanup: Some THREE.js objects may not be properly cleaned/disposed
React 18 Compatibility Issues: Doesn't properly implement getSnapshot caching

sections.title: React Component Rendering Bottlenecks
sections.content: The core components contain several rendering bottlenecks.

NeuroScene.tsx: Renders the entire 3D scene on any state change
Canvas re-creates the entire scene graph on minor updates
Multiple nested components creating memory pressure
Inefficient context propagation to child components
Usage of hooks inside render functions creating render loops
BrainModel.tsx: Model loading integrated directly in component lifecycle
Loading state affects parent component re-rendering
Potential memory leaks in THREE.js object handling
performanceMetrics: Redundant model loads for the same model ID
Component tree depth impacts render performance
Excessive prop drilling causing unnecessary renders

sections.title: 3D Model Loading Pipeline
sections.content: The model loading pipeline has several critical bottlenecks.

loadModel.ts: Inefficient path resolution with multiple fetch attempts
No proper LOD (Level of Detail) implementation
Attempts to load all model variations synchronously
Debug flags adding overhead in production builds
Overly defensive error handling causing performance degradation
dependencyManagement: THREE.js instantiation and setup happens on render
Memory management of 3D resources is inconsistent
React fiber hooks not optimized for 3D context
Model management happens in component space rather than dedicated service

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.content: The primary performance bottlenecks in the application are:
keyBottlenecks: State Management: The Zustand store architecture needs optimization for React 18
Rendering Pipeline: Component rendering cycles need better memoization
3D Asset Management: The model loading pipeline needs proper LOD implementation
Memory Management: THREE.js objects need better lifecycle handling
React Integration: Better separation of 3D and React rendering concerns needed
